statement: ▶ Problem 1. For problems such as subspace clustering and learning mixtures of Gaussians, if the relevant Ui ’s (respectively also the Vi ’s) are orthogonal to each other, does the above algorithm correctly recover the Ui ’s?
context: had the property that the Ui ’s (respectively also the Vi ’s) were orthogonal complements of each other (under some canonical inner product on  the spaces U and V ). Consider the collection of linear maps L ⊆ Lin(U, U ) defined as L := BjT · Bi : Bi , Bj ∈ B . Then each Ui is an invariant subspace (i.e. an eigenspace) of every operator in L. In such a situation we typically expect the following simple algorithm to work: simply pick three random maps B1 , B2 , B3 ∈ ⟨B⟩ and compute35 L := B2T · B1 and M := B3T · B1 . Then for each eigenvector u of L, compute the span of the orbit of u under the action of M . The distinct subspaces so obtained should typically give us the required subspaces U1 , U2 , . . . , Us . Clearly such an algorithm, when it works, would be much faster. We expect that for most applications, the above algorithm should work but we don’t know. ▶ Problem 1. For problems such as subspace clustering and learning mixtures of Gaussians, if the relevant Ui ’s (respectively also the Vi ’s) are orthogonal to each other, does the above algorithm correctly recover the Ui ’s? ▶ Problem 2. Whats the best way to make this algorithm noise-tolerant? Finally, in situations where the Ui ’s (resp the Vi ’s) are not orthogonal to each other we can clearly make them so by using appropriate inner products on U and V . But how do we find such an inner product? We expect the operator scaling algorithm of [9] to yield such an inner product(!)

Let us formally state this as an open problem. ▶ Problem 4 (Random instances of general mixtures of Gaussians.). Let n, s ≥ n be integers. For i ∈ [s] suppose that we pick µi ∈ Rn and covariance matrices Σi ∈ Rn×n independently Ps at random36 . Let D := i=1 1s · N (µi , Σi ) be the equi-weighted mixture of Gaussians with the above randomly chosen parameters. Design an efficient algorithm that given samples from D recovers the µi ’s and Σi ’s approximately.

statement: Our work as well as that of [3] leave open the problem of doing a smoothed analysis of the corresponding algorithm for mixtures of zero-mean Gaussians. To encourage this direction of research, let us state this explicitly in the form of a conjecture.
context: 35 The linear maps B2T , B3T from V to U are defined using the canonical inner products on these two spaces. 36 Any reasonable distribution would do but for concreteness say we pick µi ∼ N (0, In ) and we pick Σi = B T · B, where B ∼ N (0, 1)n×n . Our work as well as that of [3] leave open the problem of doing a smoothed analysis of the corresponding algorithm for mixtures of zero-mean Gaussians. To encourage this direction of research, let us state this explicitly in the form of a conjecture. ▶ Conjecture 6.1 (Smoothed analysis of our algorithm for mixture of zero-mean Gaussians.). Our algorithm efficiently recovers the unknown parameters for smoothed instances of mixtures of zero-mean Gaussians. Handling outliers and other applications. In Remark 1.1, we conjectured that our approach/framework should enable the design of efficient algorithms that can handle outliers and also be useful for many more applications in unsupervised learning. It would be nice to have concrete results in such directions.
